title: Anthropic ships Claude Opus 5 at half the price of Fable 5 and takes the leaderboard
subtitle: The new Opus adds a 1M-token context window, a five-level effort dial topped by a new xhigh tier, and a Fast mode — while pricing stays flat at $5/$25 per million tokens.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 on July 24, its fourth model in two months and the new flagship for coding, agents and long-horizon knowledge work. Pricing holds at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens — the same rate as Opus 4.8 and half the $10/$50 rate of Fable 5, Anthropic's most capable model. Context expands to a 1M-token window as both the default and the maximum, and max output rises to 128K tokens. On Artificial Analysis's v4.1 leaderboard, Opus 5 leads both the Intelligence Index at 61 and the Agentic Index at 55.3, ahead of Fable 5 at 60 and 52.8.

The launch also ships a new reasoning-effort dial with five levels — low, medium, high, a new xhigh above high, and an uncapped max where thinking always stays on. A separate Fast mode runs about 2.5x quicker than standard at $10/$50 per million tokens. On Frontier-Bench v0.1, Opus 5 scored 43.3 percent at maximum effort against GPT-5.6 Sol at 37.5 percent. ARC Prize verified Opus 5 at 30.2 percent on ARC-AGI-3 on launch day, roughly three times the next-best public model. On OSWorld 2.0 — a computer-use benchmark — it beats every other model at any price point and surpasses Fable 5's best score at just over a third of the cost.

The pricing move is the deeper story. For most of the last two years, frontier capability came bundled with frontier pricing — get the smartest model, pay the flagship rate. Opus 5 breaks that pairing. Anthropic is now positioning Opus as the tier where near-Fable performance is available at half the token cost, with Fable 5 reserved for the harder edge of the frontier. That mirrors the pattern Google and OpenAI have been running with mid-tier models like Gemini 3.5 Flash and GPT-5.6 Sol — capability moving down the price curve every few months, not every few years.

For learners: a rule of thumb is holding up across every lab this year — whatever the top model does today, a mid-tier model will do at roughly half the price within a quarter or two. That has direct consequences for how you build. If you are picking a model for a project you will still be running in six months, budget for the model one tier below the frontier at today's prices, and assume it will match today's frontier by the time you ship. The cost of being wrong the other way — building on the flagship and locking in flagship prices — is much higher than the cost of a mid-run upgrade.
